limitations.wanted: A urethane/TPU over-moulded or dual-extrusion tread on the wheel, printed with the AMS as a soft rolling surface
limitations.blocked_by: Only high-speed black PLA is listed as available filament, and the build has one material per part
limitations.why: A hard PLA tread on a metal track is noisier, wears faster and transmits more vibration than the original wheel's softer tread. A soft tread would make the replacement much closer to the original in feel.

limitations.wanted: A printed axle sleeve whose length exactly spans the bracket's clamping faces, so the nut clamps the bearing inner races and never the wheel
limitations.blocked_by: The bracket gap and track channel could not be measured - the person answered 'I can't measure that', so that dimension is unknown
limitations.why: It would make the design independent of whether the wheel sits between two fork plates or cantilevers off a single plate, and would guarantee the wheel is never squeezed by the nut.

limitations.wanted: Circlips or a shoulder bolt to positively retain the bearings in the wheel bore
limitations.blocked_by: Not in the hardware list - only M3-M8 socket screws, hex/lock nuts, plain washers, one M3 insert and a salvaged 1/4-20 bolt
limitations.why: The bearings would then be retained mechanically instead of by a friction press fit into printed PLA, which is the one failure mode most likely to need a reprint.
